title: Control flow: `break`, `continue`, labels and the discouraged `goto`

videos.script: Lesson 17 was about the loop itself: one keyword, for, written in three forms. This lesson is about leaving one early. {{break}} break ends a loop before its condition says so. continue skips the rest of one turn and starts the next. Each fits in a line, and each has one trap. {{trap}} The trap with break is which loop it leaves. Inside two loops, it leaves the inner one only. Inside a switch, it leaves the switch, and the loop around it carries on as if nothing happened. {{labels}} A label fixes both. You give the loop a name, and break or continue says that name. {{goto}} Go also has goto. It is legal and it is rare, and the compiler refuses the two jumps that would make it dangerous. By the end, you can point at any of these statements and say where the program goes next.
